subject: math
title: Scale Drawings: Actual Lengths, Areas, Maps and Floor Plans
seo_title: Grade 8 Scale Drawings Worksheets (Ontario Math): Free with Answer Key
standard_text: Use scale drawings to calculate actual lengths and areas, and reproduce scale drawings at different ratios
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 scale drawing worksheets for the Ontario curriculum: read scales like 1 cm : 2 m and 1:500, find actual and drawing lengths, redraw at a new scale, and find real areas from maps and floor plans. 100 math questions with an answer key.
key_big: Drawing to real: multiply by the scale. Real to drawing: divide. Area grows by the scale squared.
key_sub: 1:500 means 1 cm stands for 500 cm = 5 m. At 1 cm : 2 m, 1 cm² stands for 2 × 2 = 4 m², not 2 m².
body_html:
What a scale means

A scale drawing has the same shape as the real object, but every length is multiplied by the same number. The scale tells you how a length on the drawing compares with the real length. The drawing always comes first.

A scale can have units, like 1 cm : 5 m, or no units, like 1:500. With no units, both parts use the same unit: 1 cm stands for 500 cm, which is 5 m.

Change to a ratio

Write 1 cm : 2 m as a ratio with no units.

Use one unit: 2 m = 200 cm. So 1 cm : 200 cm.

Answer: 1:200

Actual lengths and drawing lengths

Drawing to real: multiply by the scale. Real to drawing: divide. Then check the units: 1 m = 100 cm and 1 km = 100 000 cm.

Drawing to real

A map has the scale 1:50 000. Two lakes are 4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they?

4 × 50 000 = 200 000 cm = 2000 m.

Answer: 2 km

Real to drawing

A room is 6 m long. How long is it on a 1:50 plan?

6 m = 600 cm. 600 ÷ 50 = 12.

Answer: 12 cm

To redraw at a new scale, find the real length first, then use the new scale. 6 cm at 1:100 is 600 cm in real life; at 1:200 it becomes 600 ÷ 200 = 3 cm.

Area scales by the square

When every length is multiplied by k, the area is multiplied by k × k. So change the lengths first, then find the area.

Area

A deck is 4 cm by 3 cm on a plan with the scale 1 cm : 2 m. What is its real area?

Real sides: 8 m and 6 m. Area: 8 × 6 = 48 m². (The drawing area 12 cm² × 4 = 48 also works.)

Answer: 48 m²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
1:500, so 1 cm is 500 mBoth parts use the same unit: 1 cm is 500 cm = 5 m
Scale 1 cm : 2 m, wall 10 m, so draw 20 cmReal to drawing means divide: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm
6 × 50 000 = 300 000, so 300 km300 000 cm = 3000 m = 3 km
Drawing area 12 cm² at 1 cm : 2 m is 24 m²Area grows by 2 × 2 = 4: 12 × 4 = 48 m²
1:500 has a bigger number, so it is a bigger drawing1:50 makes a larger drawing than 1:500

faq.q: What do Grade 8 students learn about scale drawings in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario Grade 8 math curriculum, students use scale drawings to calculate actual lengths and areas, and they redraw scale drawings at different ratios. Maps, floor plans and models are the usual contexts.

faq.q: How do you find the actual length from a scale drawing?
faq.a: Multiply the length on the drawing by the scale, then change the units. At 1:200, a 6 cm wall is 6 × 200 = 1200 cm, which is 12 m.

faq.q: Why does the area not scale by the same number as the lengths?
faq.a: Area uses two lengths, and both are multiplied by the scale. At 1 cm : 2 m, each 1 cm² stands for 2 m × 2 m = 4 m², so areas grow 4 times as fast as the scale number.

faq.q: How do you write 1 cm : 2 m as a ratio scale?
faq.a: Change both parts to the same unit and drop the units: 2 m = 200 cm, so 1 cm : 2 m is the ratio 1:200.

sets.title: Reading scales: 1 cm : 2 m, 1:500 and scale bars

items.q: A scale drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 2 m. What does 3 cm on the drawing stand for?
items.e: Each 1 cm stands for 2 m, so 3 cm stands for 3 × 2 = 6 m. 1.5 m divides, 5 m adds, and 6 cm forgets that the real lengths are in metres.

items.q: A plan uses the scale 1 cm : 5 m. What does 4 cm on the plan stand for?
items.e: 4 × 5 = 20 m. 0.8 m divides 4 by 5, 9 m adds 4 + 5, and 20 cm uses the wrong unit.

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 cm : 10 km. What does 7 cm on the map stand for?
items.e: 7 × 10 = 70 km. 17 km adds, 0.7 km divides, and 70 m uses metres instead of kilometres.

items.q: Each block of this scale bar is 1 cm long. What scale does it show?
items.e: The whole bar is 4 cm for 40 m. Each 1 cm block is 40 ÷ 4 = 10 m, so the scale is 1 cm : 10 m. 1 cm : 40 m reads the whole bar as 1 cm, and 1 cm : 4 m divides the wrong way.

items.q: What does the scale 1:500 mean on a plan?
c: 500 cm on the plan is 1 cm in real life
1 cm on the plan is 500 m in real life
The plan is 500 times as big as the real thing
1 cm on the plan is 500 cm in real life
items.e: A ratio scale has the same unit on both sides: 1 cm stands for 500 cm (= 5 m). The first number is the drawing, so the plan is smaller than the real thing.

items.q: Write the scale 1 cm : 2 m as a ratio with no units.
items.e: Change both parts to the same unit: 2 m = 200 cm. So 1 cm : 200 cm = 1:200. 1:2 forgets to change the metres into centimetres.

items.q: Write the map scale 1 cm : 5 km as a ratio with no units.
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m = 100 000 cm, so 5 km = 500 000 cm. The ratio is 1:500 000. 1:5000 changes km to m only.

items.q: A plan has the scale 1:500. Complete: 1 cm on the plan stands for ? in real life.
items.e: 1 cm stands for 500 cm. 500 cm ÷ 100 = 5 m. 500 m keeps the 500 but switches the unit to metres.

items.q: A plan has the scale 1:250. Complete: 1 cm on the plan stands for ? in real life.
items.e: 1 cm stands for 250 cm = 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5 m. 250 m reads the ratio as metres, and 25 m divides by 10 instead of 100.

items.q: A town map has the scale 1:20 000. Complete: 1 cm on the map stands for ? in real life.
items.e: 1 cm stands for 20 000 cm. 20 000 ÷ 100 = 200 m. 20 m divides by 1000, and 2000 m divides by 10.

items.q: A road map has the scale 1:100 000. Complete: 1 cm on the map stands for ? in real life.
items.e: 100 000 cm = 1000 m = 1 km. 100 km reads the ratio as kilometres, and 100 m divides by 1000 instead of 100.

items.q: Which scale makes a drawing that is larger than the real object?
items.e: The first number is the drawing. In 5:1, 5 cm on the drawing stands for 1 cm in real life, so the drawing is an enlargement. 1:5, 1:50 and 1:500 all make the drawing smaller.

items.q: Ethan draws the same garden at four different scales. Which scale gives the largest drawing?
items.e: At 1:50, 1 cm stands for only 50 cm, so you need more centimetres for the garden. 1:50 is the largest drawing. 1:500 has the biggest number but makes the smallest drawing.

items.q: A model car is built at a scale of 1:24. How many times as long as the model is the real car?
items.e: 1:24 means 1 cm on the model stands for 24 cm on the car. The real car is 24 times as long. 124 is how long the model is compared with the car.

items.q: A plan uses the scale 2 cm : 5 m. What does 1 cm on the plan stand for?
items.e: 2 cm stands for 5 m, so 1 cm stands for half of it: 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5 m. 10 m multiplies by 2, and 3 m subtracts 5 − 2.

items.q: A plan uses the scale 4 cm : 1 m. Write it as a ratio in the form 1:n.
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 4 cm : 100 cm. Divide both parts by 4: 1:25. 4:1 forgets to change 1 m into 100 cm.

items.q: This scale bar is 3 cm long. Which ratio does it show?
items.e: 3 cm stands for 150 m, so 1 cm stands for 50 m = 5000 cm. The ratio is 1:5000. 1:50 forgets to change metres into centimetres, and 1:150 reads the whole bar as 1 cm.

items.q: This scale bar is 2 cm long. What does 1 cm on the map stand for?
items.e: 2 cm stands for 10 km, so 1 cm stands for 10 ÷ 2 = 5 km. 2.5 km is one block, but each block is only 0.5 cm. 20 km multiplies by 2.

items.q: A floor plan has the scale 1:50. Which statement is true?
c: 1 cm on the plan stands for 50 m
1 m on the plan stands for 50 cm
2 cm on the plan stands for 1 m
50 cm on the plan stands for 1 cm
items.e: 1 cm stands for 50 cm, so 2 cm stands for 100 cm = 1 m. 50 m reads the ratio as metres, and the other two put the real length first.

items.q: Map A has the scale 1:50 000. Map B has the scale 1 cm : 2 km. Which map shows the same lake larger?
items.e: Map A: 1 cm stands for 50 000 cm = 0.5 km. Map B: 1 cm stands for 2 km. On Map A each centimetre covers less ground, so the lake is drawn larger: Map A.

items.q: The scale is 1 cm : 2 m. How long is the longer side of the real patio?
items.e: The longer side is 6 cm on the drawing. 6 × 2 = 12 m. 3 m divides, 8 m adds, and 12 cm uses the wrong unit.

items.q: The scale is 1 cm : 3 m. How wide is the real pool (the shorter side)?
items.e: The shorter side is 2 cm. 2 × 3 = 6 m. 15 m is the longer side (5 × 3), and 5 m adds 2 + 3.

items.q: A floor plan has the scale 1:200. A wall is 6 cm long on the plan. How long is the real wall?
items.e: 6 × 200 = 1200 cm. 1200 cm ÷ 100 = 12 m. 1200 m forgets to change centimetres into metres.

items.q: A plan of a house has the scale 1:50. A door is 4 cm tall on the plan. How tall is the real door?
items.e: 4 × 50 = 200 cm = 2 m. 200 m keeps 200 but changes the unit, and 0.08 m divides 4 by 50.

items.q: A hiking map has the scale 1:50 000. Two campsites are 6 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
items.e: 6 × 50 000 = 300 000 cm. 300 000 cm = 3000 m = 3 km. 300 km changes cm straight to km without dividing by 100 000.

items.q: A road map has the scale 1:250 000. Two towns are 4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
items.e: 4 × 250 000 = 1 000 000 cm = 10 000 m = 10 km. 100 km and 1 km each slip by a factor of 10 when changing units.

items.q: Two towns are 3.5 cm apart on this map. How far apart are they really?
items.e: The bar shows 4 cm for 40 km, so 1 cm stands for 10 km. 3.5 × 10 = 35 km. 140 km multiplies 3.5 by the whole bar (40 km), and 30 km drops the half centimetre.

items.q: Each square on this plan is 1 cm. The scale is 1 cm : 1.5 m. How long is the real room (the longer side)?
items.e: The longer side is 6 squares = 6 cm. 6 × 1.5 = 9 m. 7.5 m adds 6 + 1.5, 4 m divides 6 by 1.5, and 6 m forgets the scale.

items.q: Aiden builds a model car at a scale of 1:24. The model is 18 cm long. How long is the real car?
items.e: 18 × 24 = 432 cm = 4.32 m, a normal car length. 0.75 m divides 18 by 24, 43.2 m divides by 10 instead of 100, and 42 cm adds 18 + 24.

items.q: A model train is built at a scale of 1:87. The model locomotive is 20 cm long. How long is the real locomotive?
items.e: 20 × 87 = 1740 cm. 1740 ÷ 100 = 17.4 m. 174 m divides by 10 instead of 100, and 107 cm adds 20 + 87.

items.q: A plan uses the scale 2 cm : 5 m. A pool is 10 cm long on the plan. How long is the real pool?
items.e: 10 cm is 5 groups of 2 cm, so the pool is 5 × 5 = 25 m. 50 m treats the scale as 1 cm : 5 m, 4 m divides 10 by 2.5, and 20 m multiplies 10 by 2.

items.q: A bedroom plan uses the scale 1 cm : 0.5 m. The bed is 4 cm long on the plan. How long is the real bed?
items.e: 4 × 0.5 = 2 m. 8 m divides 4 by 0.5, and 4.5 m adds 4 + 0.5.

items.q: A plan uses the scale 3 cm : 1 m. A desk is 4.5 cm long on the plan. How long is the real desk?
items.e: Every 3 cm stands for 1 m, so 4.5 ÷ 3 = 1.5 m. 13.5 m multiplies by 3, 5.5 m adds 4.5 + 1, and 15 m moves the decimal point.

items.q: A science book shows an ant at a scale of 5:1. The drawing is 4 cm long. How long is the real ant?
items.e: 5:1 is an enlargement: the drawing is 5 times as long as the ant. 4 ÷ 5 = 0.8 cm = 8 mm. 20 cm multiplies, and 0.8 mm keeps the number but uses the wrong unit.

items.q: A diagram shows a ladybug at a scale of 10:1. The drawing is 50 mm long. How long is the real ladybug?
items.e: The drawing is 10 times as long as the ladybug. 50 ÷ 10 = 5 mm. 500 mm multiplies, 40 mm subtracts 10, and 0.5 mm divides by 100.

items.q: A city map has the scale 1:20 000. Two schools are 7.5 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
items.e: 7.5 × 20 000 = 150 000 cm = 1500 m = 1.5 km. 15 km and 0.15 km each slip by a factor of 10, and 150 km changes cm straight to km.

items.q: The scale is 1:100. What is the perimeter of the real classroom?
items.e: Real sides: 5 × 100 = 500 cm = 5 m and 4 × 100 = 400 cm = 4 m. Perimeter: 2 × (5 + 4) = 18 m. 9 m adds only two sides, 20 m is the area number, and 1800 m forgets to change the units.

items.q: A map has the scale 1 cm : 25 km. Toronto and Ottawa are about 14 cm apart on the map. About how far apart are they?
items.e: 14 × 25 = 350 km, close to the straight-line distance between the two cities. 39 km adds 14 + 25, and 140 km multiplies by 10.

items.q: A trail on this park map is 6 cm long. How long is the real trail?
items.e: The bar shows 4 cm for 100 m, so 1 cm stands for 25 m. 6 × 25 = 150 m. 600 m multiplies 6 by the whole bar, and 24 m multiplies 6 by 4.

items.q: A plan of a school has the scale 1:50. A hallway is 16 cm long and 3 cm wide on the plan. How much longer than wide is the real hallway?
items.e: On the plan the difference is 16 − 3 = 13 cm. 13 × 50 = 650 cm = 6.5 m. 8 m is only the real length (16 × 50 cm), and 65 m divides by 10 instead of 100.

sets.title: Drawing lengths from actual lengths, and changing the scale

items.q: A plan uses the scale 1 cm : 2 m. A real wall is 10 m long. How long is it on the plan?
items.e: Each 2 m becomes 1 cm, so divide: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm. 20 cm multiplies, 12 cm adds, and 8 cm subtracts.

items.q: A plan uses the scale 1 cm : 5 m. A real fence is 35 m long. How long is it on the plan?
items.e: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 cm. 175 cm multiplies instead of dividing, 40 cm adds, and 30 cm subtracts.

items.q: A plan has the scale 1:100. A real room is 6 m long. How long is it on the plan?
items.e: 6 m = 600 cm. 600 ÷ 100 = 6 cm. 600 cm is the real length, and 60 cm divides by 10.

items.q: A plan has the scale 1:50. A real table is 3 m long. How long is it on the plan?
items.e: 3 m = 300 cm. 300 ÷ 50 = 6 cm. 150 cm multiplies 3 by 50, and 0.6 cm and 60 cm slip by a factor of 10.

items.q: A plan has the scale 1:200. A real driveway is 15 m long. How long is it on the plan?
items.e: 15 m = 1500 cm. 1500 ÷ 200 = 7.5 cm. 3000 cm multiplies 15 by 200, and 75 cm and 0.75 cm slip by a factor of 10.

items.q: A site plan has the scale 1:500. A real parking lot is 40 m long. How long is it on the plan?
A road map has the scale 1:100 000. Two towns are 12 km apart. How far apart are they on the map?
items.e: 12 km = 1 200 000 cm. 1 200 000 ÷ 100 000 = 12 cm. Another way: 1 cm stands for 1 km, so 12 km is 12 cm.

items.q: A hiking map has the scale 1:50 000. A trail is 4 km long. How long is it on the map?
A plan uses the scale 2 cm : 1 m. A real bookshelf is 3.5 m wide. How wide is it on the plan?
items.e: Each metre becomes 2 cm: 3.5 × 2 = 7 cm. 1.75 cm divides by 2, and 5.5 cm adds 3.5 + 2.

items.q: A diagram shows a seed at a scale of 20:1. The real seed is 3 mm long. How long is it in the diagram?
items.e: 20:1 is an enlargement: the drawing is 20 times as long. 3 × 20 = 60 mm (6 cm). 0.15 mm divides, 23 mm adds, and 6 mm slips by a factor of 10.

items.q: A plan uses the scale 1 cm : 4 m. A soccer field is 100 m long. How long is it on the plan?
items.e: 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm. 400 cm multiplies, 2.5 cm divides by 40, and 96 cm subtracts.

items.q: Leah draws a garden that is 12 m by 8 m at a scale of 1:200. What size is her drawing?
items.e: 12 m = 1200 cm and 8 m = 800 cm. 1200 ÷ 200 = 6 and 800 ÷ 200 = 4: 6 cm by 4 cm. 24 cm by 16 cm multiplies by 2, and the other two slip by a factor of 10.

items.q: Ava wants to draw a 30 m by 18 m schoolyard as large as possible on a sheet 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm. Which scale should she use?
items.e: At 1:100 the drawing is 30 cm by 18 cm, too long for the sheet. At 1:200 it is 15 cm by 9 cm and fits. 1:500 (6 cm by 3.6 cm) fits too, but it is smaller. 1:50 is far too big (60 cm).

items.q: A wall is 8 cm long on a 1:100 plan. Hana redraws the plan at 1:50. How long is the wall on the new plan?
items.e: Real wall: 8 × 100 = 800 cm. At 1:50: 800 ÷ 50 = 16 cm. 1:50 is a larger scale, so the wall gets longer. 4 cm halves it instead.

items.q: A line is 9 cm long on a 1:200 drawing. Noah redraws it at 1:300. How long is the new line?
items.e: Real length: 9 × 200 = 1800 cm. At 1:300: 1800 ÷ 300 = 6 cm. 13.5 cm makes the drawing bigger, but 1:300 is a smaller scale than 1:200.

items.q: A path is 6 cm long on a plan with the scale 1 cm : 5 m. How long is it on a new plan with the scale 1 cm : 2 m?
items.e: Real path: 6 × 5 = 30 m. New plan: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm. 2.4 cm multiplies 6 by 2 and divides by 5, which is backwards, and 12 cm multiplies 6 by 2.

items.q: The CN Tower is 553 m tall. Olivia builds a model at a scale of 1:500. How tall is the model?
items.e: 553 m = 55 300 cm. 55 300 ÷ 500 = 110.6 cm, a little over 1 m. The other answers put the decimal point in the wrong place.

items.q: A floor plan uses the scale 1 cm : 0.5 m. A real room is 4.5 m long. How long is it on the plan?
items.e: Each 0.5 m becomes 1 cm. 4.5 ÷ 0.5 = 9 cm. 2.25 cm multiplies by 0.5, 5 cm adds, and 4 cm subtracts.

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 cm : 25 km. Two cities are 180 km apart. How far apart are they on the map?
items.e: 180 ÷ 25 = 7.2 cm. 4500 cm multiplies, and 0.72 cm and 72 cm slip by a factor of 10.

items.q: A hockey rink is about 61 m long. Mateo draws it at a scale of 1:500. How long is his drawing?
items.e: 61 m = 6100 cm. 6100 ÷ 500 = 12.2 cm. 30 500 cm multiplies by 500, and 1.22 cm and 122 cm slip by a factor of 10.

sets.title: Areas from scale drawings: area scales by the square

items.q: The scale is 1 cm : 3 m. What is the area of the real deck?
items.e: Change each length first: 4 × 3 = 12 m and 3 × 3 = 9 m. Area: 12 × 9 = 108 m². 36 m² multiplies the drawing area (12) by 3 only once, and 42 is the real perimeter.

items.q: The scale is 1 cm : 3 m. What is the area of the real garden?
items.e: Real sides: 5 × 3 = 15 m and 2 × 3 = 6 m. Area: 15 × 6 = 90 m². 30 m² multiplies 10 cm² by 3 instead of 3 × 3 = 9, and 42 is the real perimeter.

items.q: A plan has the scale 1:100. A square on the plan is 1 cm by 1 cm. What real area does it stand for?
items.e: 1 cm stands for 100 cm = 1 m, so the square stands for 1 m by 1 m = 1 m². 100 cm² scales the area by 100 instead of 100 × 100 = 10 000.

items.q: Every length in a drawing is made 3 times as long. How many times as large is the area?
items.e: Length and width are both 3 times as long, so the area is 3 × 3 = 9 times as large. 3 forgets that both sides change, and 27 is 3 × 3 × 3 (that is for volume).

items.q: A plan uses the scale 1 cm : 2 m. What real area does 1 cm² on the plan stand for?
items.e: 1 cm by 1 cm stands for 2 m by 2 m = 4 m². 2 m² scales the area like a length, and 8 m² is 2 × 2 × 2.

items.q: A plan uses the scale 1 cm : 5 m. A lawn covers 6 cm² on the plan. What is the real area of the lawn?
items.e: Each 1 cm² stands for 5 × 5 = 25 m². 6 × 25 = 150 m². 30 m² multiplies by 5 only once, and 11 adds 6 + 5.

items.q: Each square on this plan is 1 cm. The scale is 1 cm : 1.5 m. What is the area of the real room?
items.e: Real sides: 4 × 1.5 = 6 m and 3 × 1.5 = 4.5 m. Area: 6 × 4.5 = 27 m². 18 m² multiplies 12 squares by 1.5 only once, and 21 is the real perimeter.

items.q: Each square on this L-shaped plan is 1 cm. The scale is 1 cm : 2 m. What is the area of the real room?
items.e: The room covers 10 squares = 10 cm². Each 1 cm² stands for 2 × 2 = 4 m². 10 × 4 = 40 m². 20 m² multiplies by 2 only once.

items.q: A map has the scale 1:100 000. A lake covers 3 cm² on the map. What is the real area of the lake?
items.e: 1 cm stands for 100 000 cm = 1 km, so 1 cm² stands for 1 km × 1 km = 1 km². 3 cm² stands for 3 km².

items.q: A map has the scale 1:50 000. A park covers 8 cm² on the map. What is the real area of the park?
items.e: 1 cm stands for 0.5 km, so 1 cm² stands for 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25 km². 8 × 0.25 = 2 km². 4 km² multiplies 8 by 0.5 only once, and 0.25 km² is just one square centimetre.

items.q: A patio has an area of 24 m². How much area does it cover on a plan with the scale 1 cm : 2 m?
items.e: Each 1 cm² stands for 2 × 2 = 4 m². 24 ÷ 4 = 6 cm². 12 cm² divides by 2 only once, and 48 and 96 multiply instead of dividing.

items.q: A plan has the scale 1:50. A room covers 40 cm² on the plan. What is the real area of the room?
items.e: 1 cm² stands for 50 × 50 = 2500 cm². 40 × 2500 = 100 000 cm² = 10 m² (1 m² = 10 000 cm²). 0.2 m² multiplies by 50 only once.

items.q: The same garden is drawn at 1:100 and at 1:200. How does its area on the 1:200 drawing compare with its area on the 1:100 drawing?
items.e: At 1:200 every length is half as long as at 1:100. The area is 12 × 12 = 14 as large. 12 scales the area like a length.

items.q: A photo 10 cm by 15 cm is enlarged so that every length is twice as long. What is the area of the new photo?
items.e: New photo: 20 cm by 30 cm = 600 cm², which is 2 × 2 = 4 times the old 150 cm². 300 cm² only doubles the area.

items.q: Drawing B of a room has 4 times the area of drawing A. How many times as long is each side in drawing B?
items.e: Area grows by the square of the length factor. 2 × 2 = 4, so each side is 2 times as long. 4 would make the area 16 times as large.

items.q: A rectangular lot is 20 m by 15 m. What area does it cover on a 1:500 plan?
items.e: 20 m = 2000 cm and 15 m = 1500 cm. On the plan: 2000 ÷ 500 = 4 cm and 1500 ÷ 500 = 3 cm. Area: 4 × 3 = 12 cm². 0.6 divides 300 m² by 500 only once.

items.q: The scale is 1:50. What is the area of the real shed floor?
items.e: Real sides: 6 × 50 = 300 cm = 3 m and 4 × 50 = 200 cm = 2 m. Area: 3 × 2 = 6 m². 0.12 m² multiplies 24 cm² by 50 only once.

items.q: A rug is 2 m by 3 m. Kai draws it on a plan with the scale 1 cm : 0.5 m. What area does the rug cover on the plan?
items.e: On the plan: 2 ÷ 0.5 = 4 cm and 3 ÷ 0.5 = 6 cm. Area: 4 × 6 = 24 cm². 12 cm² divides the 6 m² by 0.5 only once, and 1.5 cm² multiplies by 0.5 × 0.5.

items.q: A plan uses the scale 1 cm : 10 m. A field covers 5 cm² on the plan. What is the real area of the field?
items.e: Each 1 cm² stands for 10 × 10 = 100 m². 5 × 100 = 500 m². 50 m² multiplies by 10 only once.

items.q: A rectangular room has an area of 72 m², and its long side is 12 m. How wide is the room on a 1:200 plan?
items.e: Real width: 72 ÷ 12 = 6 m = 600 cm. On the plan: 600 ÷ 200 = 3 cm. 6 cm is the long side on the plan (1200 ÷ 200), and 0.36 cm divides the area by 200.

sets.title: Word problems: maps, floor plans and models

items.q: Zoe’s family plans a canoe trip in Algonquin Park. On a 1:50 000 map, the route is 9 cm long. They paddle at about 3 km/h. About how long will the trip take?
items.e: Real route: 9 × 50 000 = 450 000 cm = 4.5 km. Time: 4.5 ÷ 3 = 1.5 h. 15 h comes from 45 km (a units slip), and 4.5 is the distance, not the time.

items.q: A bedroom is 8 cm by 7 cm on a plan with the scale 1 cm : 0.5 m. Carpet costs $30 per square metre. What does carpet for the whole floor cost?
items.e: Real room: 4 m by 3.5 m = 14 m². 14 × $30 = $420. $840 scales the 56 cm² by 0.5 only once, $1680 forgets the scale, and $450 uses the perimeter (15 m).

items.q: A Toronto street map uses the scale 1 cm : 250 m. Arjun’s school and the library are 12 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
items.e: 12 × 250 = 3000 m = 3 km. 300 m drops a zero, and 30 km adds one.

items.q: A real canoe is 5 m long. Owen builds a model at a scale of 1:20. How long is the model?
items.e: 5 m = 500 cm. 500 ÷ 20 = 25 cm. 100 cm multiplies 5 by 20, and 2.5 cm divides by 200.

items.q: Emma draws her vegetable garden as a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle with the scale 1 cm : 0.5 m. Fencing costs $12 per metre. What does a fence all the way around cost?
items.e: Real garden: 3 m by 2 m. Perimeter: 2 × (3 + 2) = 10 m. 10 × $12 = $120. $240 uses the 20 cm perimeter on the drawing, $72 uses the 6 m² area, and $288 uses 24 cm².

items.q: An elevation drawing of a wall has the scale 1:50. The wall is 8 cm by 5 cm on the drawing. What is the real area of the wall to be painted?
items.e: Real wall: 8 × 50 = 400 cm = 4 m and 5 × 50 = 250 cm = 2.5 m. Area: 4 × 2.5 = 10 m². 0.2 m² multiplies 40 cm² by 50 only once, and 26 is a perimeter in centimetres.

items.q: Two towns are 6 cm apart on a 1:100 000 map. How far apart are they on a 1:250 000 map?
items.e: Real distance: 6 × 100 000 cm = 6 km. On the new map: 600 000 ÷ 250 000 = 2.4 cm. 15 cm makes the distance bigger, but 1:250 000 is a smaller scale.

items.q: Hana draws a 60 m by 26 m hockey rink at the scale 1 cm : 2 m on a sheet 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm. Will the drawing fit?
c: Yes: it would be 15 cm long
Yes: it would be 6 cm long
No: it would be 120 cm long
No: it would be 30 cm long
items.e: 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm, which is longer than 27.9 cm, so no. 120 cm multiplies by 2, 15 cm divides 60 by 4, and 6 cm divides 60 by 10.

items.q: A cottage plan has the scale 1:100. The living room is 5.5 cm by 4 cm on the plan. What is its real area?
items.e: Real room: 5.5 m by 4 m. Area: 5.5 × 4 = 22 m². 0.22 m² multiplies 22 cm² by 100 only once, and 19 is the real perimeter.

items.q: Jayden’s hike is 7 cm long on this trail map. How long is the real hike?
items.e: The bar shows 4 cm for 2 km, so 1 cm stands for 0.5 km. 7 × 0.5 = 3.5 km. 14 km multiplies 7 by the whole bar, and 1.75 km divides 7 by 4.

items.q: A building lot is 6 cm by 9 cm on a 1:500 plan. What is the real area of the lot?
items.e: Real lot: 6 × 5 m = 30 m and 9 × 5 m = 45 m. Area: 30 × 45 = 1350 m². 27 000 m² multiplies 54 cm² by 500 and keeps the wrong unit, and 150 is the real perimeter.

items.q: A classroom is 9 m long. On Benjamin’s plan it is 18 cm long. What scale did he use?
items.e: Use the same unit: 9 m = 900 cm. 18 : 900 = 1 : 50, so the scale is 1:50. 1:2 and 2:1 compare 18 and 9 without changing the units.

items.q: Two towns 24 km apart are 8 cm apart on a map. What is the scale of the map?
items.e: 8 cm stands for 24 km, so 1 cm stands for 3 km = 300 000 cm. The scale is 1:300 000. 1:3 forgets to change km into cm.

items.q: Priya’s model of her school has the scale 1:200. The gym floor is 15 cm by 10 cm on the model. What is the area of the real gym floor?
items.e: Real gym: 15 × 200 = 3000 cm = 30 m and 10 × 200 = 2000 cm = 20 m. Area: 30 × 20 = 600 m². 3 m² multiplies 150 cm² by 200 only once, and 100 is the real perimeter.

items.q: A city park plan has the scale 1:1000. A soccer field is 10 cm by 6.5 cm on the plan. What is the area of the real field?
items.e: 1 cm stands for 1000 cm = 10 m. Real field: 100 m by 65 m. Area: 100 × 65 = 6500 m². 65 m² treats each 1 cm² as 1 m², 65 000 m² multiplies 65 by 1000, and 330 is the real perimeter.

items.q: Maya enlarges a 4 cm by 6 cm photo of a loon so that the 4 cm side becomes 12 cm. How long is the other side now?
items.e: 4 cm became 12 cm, so the scale factor is 12 ÷ 4 = 3. 6 × 3 = 18 cm. 14 cm adds 8 to both sides, and 54 cm multiplies by 9, the area factor.

items.q: On a 1:5 000 000 map, Toronto and Montréal are about 10 cm apart. About how far apart are they in a straight line?
A kitchen is 6 cm by 5 cm on a plan with the scale 1 cm : 0.5 m. Each floor tile is 0.5 m by 0.5 m. How many tiles cover the floor?
items.e: Real kitchen: 3 m by 2.5 m, so 6 tiles by 5 tiles = 30 tiles. Each 1 cm square on the plan is one tile. 15 multiplies 30 cm² by 0.5, and 8 rounds up the 7.5 m² area.

items.q: A sugar shack has a floor area of 48 m². How much area does the floor cover on a 1:400 plan?
items.e: 1 cm stands for 400 cm = 4 m, so 1 cm² stands for 4 × 4 = 16 m². 48 ÷ 16 = 3 cm². 12 cm² divides by 4 only once, and 192 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Amira’s map has the scale 1:25 000 and Lucas’s map has the scale 1:50 000. A lake covers 3 cm² on Lucas’s map. How much area does it cover on Amira’s map?
items.e: Amira’s map is twice as large in every length, so areas are 2 × 2 = 4 times as large: 3 × 4 = 12 cm². 6 cm² doubles the area only once, and 1.5 cm² and 0.75 cm² make it smaller.
